questions.question: How many carpal bones make up the carpus?
questions.explanation: The carpus consists of eight carpal bones.

questions.question: In how many rows are the carpal bones arranged?
questions.explanation: The carpal bones are arranged in two rows: proximal and distal.

questions.question: How many bones are in each carpal row?
questions.explanation: Each row consists of four bones.

questions.question: Which bone is located most laterally in the proximal row?
questions.explanation: The proximal row from lateral to medial begins with the scaphoid.

questions.question: Which bone is located most medially in the proximal row?
questions.explanation: The proximal row from lateral to medial ends with the pisiform.

questions.question: Which bone is located most laterally in the distal row?
questions.explanation: The distal row from lateral to medial begins with the trapezium.

questions.question: Which bone is located most medially in the distal row?
questions.explanation: The distal row from lateral to medial ends with the hamate.

questions.question: Which carpal bone is described as boat-shaped?
questions.explanation: The scaphoid is identified as boat-shaped.

questions.question: Which carpal bone is described as moon-shaped?
questions.explanation: The lunate is identified as moon-shaped or crescentic.

questions.question: Which carpal bone is described as pyramidal in shape?
questions.explanation: The triquetral bone is described as pyramidal in shape.

questions.question: Which carpal bone is described as pea-shaped?
questions.explanation: The pisiform is identified as pea-shaped or pea-like.

questions.question: Which carpal bone has a groove and crest on its palmar surface?
questions.explanation: The trapezium is quadrilateral and has a groove and crest on its palmar surface.

questions.question: Which carpal bone is described as shoe-shaped?
questions.explanation: The trapezoid bone is identified as shoe-shaped.

questions.question: Which is the largest carpal bone?
questions.explanation: The capitate is identified as the largest carpal bone.

questions.question: Which carpal bone features a hook-like process?
questions.explanation: The hamate is wedge-shaped and has a hook-like process on its palmar surface.

questions.question: Which carpal bone has a rounded head on its proximal surface?
questions.explanation: The capitate has a rounded head on its proximal surface.

questions.question: What is the morphological origin of the pisiform bone?
questions.explanation: The pisiform is usually regarded as a sesamoid bone developed in the tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris.

questions.question: Which carpal bone is the most commonly fractured?
questions.explanation: Fracture of the scaphoid is the most common fracture of the carpus.

questions.question: A scaphoid fracture usually occurs due to which mechanism?
questions.explanation: Scaphoid fractures usually occur due to a fall on the outstretched hand.

questions.question: At which part does the scaphoid bone usually fracture?
questions.explanation: The fracture occurs at the narrow waist of the scaphoid.

questions.question: Tenderness in which area clinically indicates a scaphoid fracture?
questions.explanation: Clinically, a scaphoid fracture presents as tenderness in the anatomical box.

questions.question: Which complication can occur if the proximal segment of a fractured scaphoid loses its blood supply?
questions.explanation: If the proximal segment is deprived of blood supply, it may undergo avascular necrosis.

questions.question: What is the state of the carpal bones at birth?
questions.explanation: The carpal bones are cartilaginous at birth.

questions.question: How many ossification centers does each carpal bone have?
questions.explanation: Each carpal bone ossifies by one centre and all these centres appear after birth.

questions.question: Which carpal bone is the first to ossify?
questions.explanation: The capitate is the first bone to ossify in the carpus.

questions.question: Which carpal bone is the last to ossify?
questions.explanation: The pisiform is the last bone to ossify in the carpus.

questions.question: At what age does the ossification center for the capitate appear?
questions.explanation: The center for the capitate appears during the second month.

questions.question: At what age does the ossification center for the hamate appear?
questions.explanation: The center for the hamate appears at the end of the third month.

questions.question: In females, at what age does the pisiform bone typically ossify?
questions.explanation: The pisiform ossifies in the 9th to 10th year in females.

questions.question: Knowledge of carpal bone ossification is important for determining what?
questions.explanation: The knowledge of ossification of carpal bones is important in determining the bone age of the child.
